newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Sungei Way assessing Cambodia situation.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Sungei Way assessing Cambodia situation.

text.p: Malaysian construction and property concern Sungei Way group said on Wednesday it is assessing the situation in Cambodia before making any further investments.

"We will need to assess the situation carefully before making any further financial commitments in this country as our overseas investment strategies remain to be very much market driven," the group said in a statement.
It added, "on a longer-term basis, we are still positive on the group's investment in Cambodia."
Fighting earlier this month between forces of Cambodia's two premiers resulted in the overthrow of First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, with Second Prime Minister Hun Sen seizing power.
Hundreds of Malaysians employed in Cambodia were evacuated last week along with other foreigners.

Sungei Way group's involvement in Cambodia is through property developer Sunway City Bhd, which is conducting feasibility studies for a 1.25 billion ringgit ($500 million) 400 ha satellite town on the outskirts of Phnom Penh.
Sungei Way said Sunway City has not made any financial commitments toward the project.

Sunway City has spent about 10 million ringgit on a three-star hotel project in Phnom Penh. "Given the current situation, the hotel which is supposed to be opened later this year will probably be slightly delayed," the statement said.
"The hotel building so far has not been affected by the civil disturbances," the statement added.
